verdict: Caution on new Guwahati residential developer exposure until cost and approval timelines are re-underwritten; lend selectively to completed-inventory and mid-income builders with escrow discipline, avoid land-heavy and pre-launch-dependent borrowers.
title: Guwahati residential real estate: a note to the credit manager
narrative:
**Cash sits in customer advances and unsold inventory, not in the P&L.** Cost is land, cement-steel-labour, and approval delay; pricing power is thin because buyers compare projects within a few kilometres. So when a proposal lands, check the sales-to-construction-cost ratio and the share of cost already collected from buyers; if collections lag construction spend, ask which project funds the gap. ## What has changed now
Local reporting says AREIDA has flagged soaring costs and policy lapses, with West Asia unrest causing cost overruns and completion delays in Guwahati [3]. Separately, the Assam Minister has reviewed building rules with realty bodies [1], which means approval norms may move. **Cost inflation plus rule revision is a margin and timeline problem, not a demand problem.** Note [3] is dated June 2026 and [1] October 2026; both are local news, not audited numbers. The data pack gives no city score [D], so I am leaning on first principles and peers. ## Where the growth is
Peer results show the national residential cycle still clearing inventory: Brigade reported Q2 profit up 29% to Rs 219 crore on sales of Rs 1,827 crore, with 2.4 million sq ft launched [4], and plans over 7 million sq ft of launches in H2 FY27 [6]. **Pursue Guwahati builders with completed or near-completed stock and a mid-income ticket, not pre-launch-heavy plotted schemes.** Avoid borrowers whose repayment depends on launching new phases before the current one is sold; their cash cycle is the one [3] describes as delayed. ## How to grow safely
Structure against receivables and escrow, not land value. **Take monthly: project-wise collection statement, construction cost incurred versus certified, RERA escrow balance, unsold inventory count, and approval status.** Covenant that customer advances stay in the project account and that no new phase launches until the prior phase crosses a collection threshold you set with the borrower. If the borrower cannot produce project-wise collections, collect from customer before sanction. ## Early-warning signs
- Monthly collection versus construction spend (monthly): two consecutive months of spend exceeding collection -> freeze further disbursement and re-cut the schedule. - RERA escrow withdrawal pattern (monthly): withdrawals ahead of certified progress -> ask for engineer certificate and stop next tranche. - Approval status per project (quarterly): any rule change under [1] hitting a live project -> re-price timeline and extend only against fresh sales evidence. - Unsold inventory ageing (monthly): rising finished-but-unsold units -> shift to completion-linked lending only.
